statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: The assessment placed most coastal homes, tourist lodging and utility lines within 30 metres of Melekeok’s high-water mark, vulnerable to sea rise, waves and typhoons.
compact_statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: The assessment placed most coastal homes, tourist lodging and utility lines within 30 metres of Melekeok’s high-water mark, vulnerable to sea rise, waves and typhoons.
scenario: The 2013 assessment considers sea-level rise, storm surge and waves through 2100.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 43–44 (printed pp. 44–45), Melekeok vulnerability assessment.

uncertainty: 2013 estimate for the mapped coastal strip.

statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: It identified the southern-coast wastewater plant as a low-lying mangrove-edge asset at risk of inundation, damage and sewage release.
compact_statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: It identified the southern-coast wastewater plant as a low-lying mangrove-edge asset at risk of inundation, damage and sewage release.
scenario: Projected sea-level rise and storm surge.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 44 (printed p. 45), Melekeok coastal wastewater-treatment plant assessment.

uncertainty: Projected risk, not a reported failure.

statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: Ngardok Nature Reserve covers one-third of Melekeok and supplies its only drinking water; prolonged drought is identified as its greatest natural-system threat, alongside flood and erosion risks.
compact_statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: Ngardok Nature Reserve covers one-third of Melekeok and supplies its only drinking water; prolonged drought is identified as its greatest natural-system threat, alongside flood and erosion risks.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 44 (printed p. 45), Ngardok Nature Reserve and water-supply assessment.

uncertainty: Risks are not quantified as service or household impacts.

statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: Proposed outputs included resilient wastewater, watershed and water-supply systems plus a state adaptation plan; no project adaptation strategies had yet been implemented.
compact_statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: Proposed outputs included resilient wastewater, watershed and water-supply systems plus a state adaptation plan; no project adaptation strategies had yet been implemented.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 44–45 (printed pp. 45–46), Melekeok assessment outputs and implementation status.

uncertainty: 2013 recommendations and status; later implementation was not checked.

statement: The 2025 water policy identifies the Ngerikiil catchment in Airai as the primary supply area for Airai and Koror. Its population-coverage figures vary between passages, so the bank retains qualitative dependence rather than a precise current coverage share.
compact_statement: The 2025 water policy identifies the Ngerikiil catchment in Airai as the primary supply area for Airai and Koror. Its population-coverage figures vary between passages, so the bank retains qualitative dependence rather than a precise current coverage share.
uncertainty: The policy reports 75% on one-based PDF p. 8 and about 80% on p. 21. Scope/vintage differences are unresolved; these are not independently verified current outage or service-coverage estimates.

statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The policy says households on remote atolls including Kayangel, Sonsorol and Hatohobei mostly rely on rainwater catchments rather than piped treated water.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The policy says households on remote atolls including Kayangel, Sonsorol and Hatohobei mostly rely on rainwater catchments rather than piped treated water.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 20, section 6.1.1, outlying-island supply paragraph.

uncertainty: The policy does not give atoll-specific household counts or catchment reliability data.

statement: Source dated 2025 reports: While Koror–Airai water quality is described as good, small rural Babeldaob plants often have high turbidity after heavy rain and sometimes detect E. coli or coliforms.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: While Koror–Airai water quality is described as good, small rural Babeldaob plants often have high turbidity after heavy rain and sometimes detect E. coli or coliforms.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 20, Koror–Airai and rural Babeldaob water-treatment descriptions.

uncertainty: Policy describes common service conditions but provides no measured prevalence by village.

statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The policy records that the 2016 drought brought water shortages, poor sanitation, crop failures and malnutrition risk; it also says utility financial shortfalls prevent needed quality improvements in smaller systems.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The policy records that the 2016 drought brought water shortages, poor sanitation, crop failures and malnutrition risk; it also says utility financial shortfalls prevent needed quality improvements in smaller systems.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 11 and 22, drought/water-resource and utility-finance sections.

uncertainty: Drought conditions are from 2016; the policy does not quantify current household-level effects.

statement: Source dated 2021 reports: At Iporu on Tobi, surveyors found erosion had exposed archaeological remains; low-lying Tobi cultural sites (3–4 metres and below) were considered at risk of inundation.
compact_statement: Source dated 2021 reports: At Iporu on Tobi, surveyors found erosion had exposed archaeological remains; low-lying Tobi cultural sites (3–4 metres and below) were considered at risk of inundation.
affected_groups: Palauan communities with cultural ties to Tobi
institutions: Bureau of Cultural and Historical Preservation
scenario: Projected inundation risk; no sea-level scenario is specified.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2, executive summary; pp. 22–23, Iporu/Tobi site assessment and recommendations.

uncertainty: Selected heritage sites, not a representative household study.

statement: Source dated 2021 reports: The report describes 2012–13 typhoon-driven debris, saltwater inundation affecting Kayangel gardens and homes, and flooding again in April 2021 at the low-lying traditional-village sites.
compact_statement: Source dated 2021 reports: The report describes 2012–13 typhoon-driven debris, saltwater inundation affecting Kayangel gardens and homes, and flooding again in April 2021 at the low-lying traditional-village sites.
institutions: Bureau of Cultural and Historical Preservation

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 24–27, Kayangel traditional-village assessment and recommendations.

uncertainty: The source documents site and event conditions; it does not attribute individual storms to climate change.

statement: Source dated 2021 reports: At the Melekeok coast, four stone monoliths had been undercut by erosion and were resting on the beach; the report recommends restoring and reinforcing the site and keeping a drainage culvert clear.
compact_statement: Source dated 2021 reports: At the Melekeok coast, four stone monoliths had been undercut by erosion and were resting on the beach; the report recommends restoring and reinforcing the site and keeping a drainage culvert clear.
institutions: Bureau of Cultural and Historical Preservation

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 33–34, Odalmelech monolith assessment in Melekeok State.

uncertainty: Historical erosion of a named cultural site and proposed restoration; completed restoration or effective adaptation is not verified.

statement: Source dated 2023-11-03 reports: The Rock Islands Southern Lagoon resilience strategy was co-designed over two years by the local management authority and community with NGO and scientific partners, drawing on reef-condition data and community dependence on reef resources.
compact_statement: Source dated 2023-11-03 reports: The Rock Islands Southern Lagoon resilience strategy was co-designed over two years by the local management authority and community with NGO and scientific partners, drawing on reef-condition data and community dependence on reef resources.
institutions: Rock Islands Southern Lagoon management authority

source_refs.locator: UNESCO page, paragraphs describing strategy design and community dependence on the reef.

uncertainty: UNESCO programme account; it does not quantify how many households depend on the reef.

statement: Source dated 2023-11-03 reports: The strategy account says earlier plans lacked implementation funds and integration; its first phase includes cultural-site preservation, sustainable fisheries, conservation finance and adaptive-management capacity, with a resilience officer placed in Koror State Government.
compact_statement: Source dated 2023-11-03 reports: The strategy account says earlier plans lacked implementation funds and integration; its first phase includes cultural-site preservation, sustainable fisheries, conservation finance and adaptive-management capacity, with a resilience officer placed in Koror State Government.

source_refs.locator: UNESCO page, strategy implementation and financing paragraphs.

uncertainty: Strategy outputs and staffing are reported; no outcome evaluation is presented.

statement: Source dated 2023-11-03 reports: The local authority adopted a 2021 coastal-fisheries plan applying traditional knowledge to reef-fish and invertebrate recovery and sustainable harvesting for the Koror community.
compact_statement: Source dated 2023-11-03 reports: The local authority adopted a 2021 coastal-fisheries plan applying traditional knowledge to reef-fish and invertebrate recovery and sustainable harvesting for the Koror community.
institutions: Rock Islands Southern Lagoon management authority

source_refs.locator: UNESCO page, paragraph on coastal fisheries management plan adopted in 2021.

uncertainty: The plan is reported as adopted; the publisher page gives no measured ecological or livelihood outcomes.

statement: Source dated not stated reports: The Office of Climate Change says the PCCP 2025 covers nine sectors and five pillars and is accompanied by a ten-year action plan developed through a two-year process involving 150-plus people.
compact_statement: Source dated not stated reports: The Office of Climate Change says the PCCP 2025 covers nine sectors and five pillars and is accompanied by a ten-year action plan developed through a two-year process involving 150-plus people.

source_refs.locator: Official climate-office page, Palau Climate Change Policy section.

uncertainty: Official page summarizes policy architecture; the action plan's delivery is not evaluated there.

statement: Source dated not stated reports: The Office page projects annual widespread coral bleaching by 2040 and stronger typhoon intensity; it says rising sea level will worsen high-tide flooding, storm surge and erosion.
compact_statement: Source dated not stated reports: The Office page projects annual widespread coral bleaching by 2040 and stronger typhoon intensity; it says rising sea level will worsen high-tide flooding, storm surge and erosion.
scenario: The official webpage gives these projections but does not identify an emissions scenario.

source_refs.locator: Official climate-office page, ‘Key Climate Impacts in Palau’ sections on reefs, storms and sea level.

uncertainty: Official webpage's forward-looking claims without reported projection methods/scenario; annual widespread bleaching by 2040 is not observed frequency or an unqualified prediction.

statement: Source dated 2020-02-06 reports: UNDP reports Typhoon Haiyan caused severe multi-sector infrastructure damage in Palau in 2013, with an estimated 454 homes destroyed or damaged.
compact_statement: Source dated 2020-02-06 reports: UNDP reports Typhoon Haiyan caused severe multi-sector infrastructure damage in Palau in 2013, with an estimated 454 homes destroyed or damaged.

source_refs.locator: UNDP page, paragraph reporting Typhoon Haiyan damage in 2013.

uncertainty: National historical estimate; the report does not attribute this typhoon to climate change.

statement: Source dated 2020-02-06 reports: UNDP says the 2016 El Niño drought caused water shortages across 80% of Palau and sanitation risks; NEMO noted the country’s remoteness delays resources and that assessment training can improve response planning.
compact_statement: Source dated 2020-02-06 reports: UNDP says the 2016 El Niño drought caused water shortages across 80% of Palau and sanitation risks; NEMO noted the country’s remoteness delays resources and that assessment training can improve response planning.

source_refs.locator: UNDP page, paragraphs on the 2016 El Niño drought and remoteness-related response planning.

uncertainty: UNDP's dated account of 2016 drought and remoteness-related response constraints, not current water coverage or evaluated training effectiveness.

statement: Source dated 2020-02-06 reports: A February 2020 UNDP–SPC–NEMO partnership planned five-day post-disaster assessment and recovery training for 30 officials and stakeholders, 40% women, across sectors including gender, water, health and housing.
compact_statement: Source dated 2020-02-06 reports: A February 2020 UNDP–SPC–NEMO partnership planned five-day post-disaster assessment and recovery training for 30 officials and stakeholders, 40% women, across sectors including gender, water, health and housing.
